title: Use only approved AI tools
outcome: Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
why: Both ask for a maintained inventory of the AI systems in use, decided before use rather than after.

title: Use only approved AI tools
outcome: Resources for AI systems
why: The Resources category covers documenting the AI systems and tooling an organization relies on; the rule covers only the approved-tool list.

title: Keep sensitive information out of AI tools
outcome: Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.
why: The rule keeps sensitive data out of unapproved tools, which is one way to limit the privacy risk this subcategory asks to be examined.

title: Keep sensitive information out of AI tools
outcome: Use of AI systems
why: Use of AI systems covers responsible-use processes; keeping data classes out of tools is one such process.

title: A person approves before AI-drafted work goes out
outcome: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.
why: Both require a defined, documented process for a person to oversee AI output, here an approver before anything goes out.

title: A person approves before AI-drafted work goes out
outcome: Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
why: The named approver is a defined human role over AI output; the subcategory also asks for policies that differentiate human-AI configurations.

title: A person approves before AI-drafted work goes out
outcome: Use of AI systems
why: Use of AI systems covers responsible-use processes, of which human approval of output is one.

title: Check drafts against a written list of things you never publish
outcome: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system’s capability, established context, and AI system categorization.
why: A written never-publish list fixes the scope of what AI-drafted output may be used for.

title: Check drafts against a written list of things you never publish
outcome: The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
why: The list writes the organization's own trustworthiness lines into a policy that is then checked against drafts.

title: Check drafts against a written list of things you never publish
outcome: Use of AI systems
why: Use of AI systems covers boundaries on intended and responsible use, of which a never-publish list is one.

title: Keep public-facing AI output nonpartisan
outcome: Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.
why: Neutrality on elections is a legal duty for many public bodies; the subcategory asks that such requirements be understood and documented.

title: Keep public-facing AI output nonpartisan
outcome: Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: the specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; and related TEVV and system metrics.
why: Context-specific norms and expectations for a public body are part of the deployment context this subcategory asks to be documented.

title: Keep public-facing AI output nonpartisan
outcome: Assessing impacts of AI systems
why: Assessing impacts covers societal impact of AI systems; a nonpartisan rule guards one societal impact of public-body output.

title: Say when AI is involved, and never fake a person
outcome: Risks associated with transparency and accountability – as identified in the MAP function – are examined and documented.
why: Disclosing AI involvement addresses a transparency risk; the subcategory asks that such risks be examined and documented, which the rule does not require.

title: Say when AI is involved, and never fake a person
outcome: Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.
why: Telling people when AI is involved is communicating about the impact of AI use more broadly.

title: Say when AI is involved, and never fake a person
outcome: Information for interested parties of AI systems
why: Information for interested parties covers telling people they are dealing with AI and about its outputs.

title: Check facts and sources before you rely on AI output
outcome: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context – as identified in the MAP function – to inform responsible use and governance.
why: A person checking output against the source is interpreting AI output in context before relying on it.

title: Check facts and sources before you rely on AI output
outcome: Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making decisions and taking subsequent actions.
why: The rule treats AI output as fallible and subject to human checking, which presupposes documented knowledge limits.

title: Check facts and sources before you rely on AI output
outcome: Use of AI systems
why: Use of AI systems covers responsible-use processes, of which verifying output before reliance is one.

title: Put a spending cap on paid AI
why: The AI RMF has no subcategory on cost or budget; a spending ceiling is financial control, not one of its trustworthiness or risk outcomes. MANAGE 2.4 was considered and rejected because it concerns performance inconsistent with intended use, not spend.

title: Put a spending cap on paid AI
why: No publicly listed clause or Annex A control title is about cost limits on AI use; Resources for AI systems concerns having and documenting resources, not capping them.

title: Limit how much the public can use your AI tool
outcome: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
why: Per-person and total limits protect a public tool from abuse and exhaustion, which is part of its security and resilience.

title: Limit how much the public can use your AI tool
why: No publicly listed clause or control title is about throttling a public AI service.

title: Keep keys and passwords in one secure store
outcome: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
why: Keeping keys in one secure store is a security control for the AI system and its connections.

title: Keep keys and passwords in one secure store
why: Credential handling is an information-security control, which ISO/IEC 42001 leaves to its companion ISO/IEC 27001 rather than listing in its own Annex A.

title: Give AI tools the least access they need
outcome: AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.
why: Granting only the permissions an approved use needs limits what a compromised AI connection can reach.

title: Give AI tools the least access they need
why: Access permissions are an information-security control, which ISO/IEC 42001 leaves to ISO/IEC 27001 rather than listing in its own Annex A.

title: Keep an off switch anyone on duty can use
outcome: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
why: Both require a mechanism, with assigned responsibility, to stop an AI process that is acting outside its intended use.

title: Keep an off switch anyone on duty can use
outcome: Operation
why: Operation covers planning and controlling AI processes in running use; an off switch is one such control.

title: Keep a record of what AI did
outcome: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.
why: A record of which tool did what is the raw material for monitoring AI behavior in production; the rule does not itself require the monitoring.

title: Keep a record of what AI did
outcome: AI system life cycle
why: The life cycle category covers recording events from AI system operation; the rule asks for a lighter organizational record.

title: Watch for automations that quietly stop working
outcome: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.
why: Both ask that AI functionality be checked while running in production, not only that no error was raised.

title: Watch for automations that quietly stop working
outcome: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.
why: A scheduled check that each automation still works is part of a post-deployment monitoring plan.

title: Watch for automations that quietly stop working
outcome: AI system operation and monitoring
why: The control is titled operation and monitoring of the AI system; the rule is the monitoring half, for automations.

title: Watch for automations that quietly stop working
outcome: Performance evaluation
why: Performance evaluation covers monitoring and measuring the management system; the rule monitors the automations it governs.

title: Name an owner and review this policy on a schedule
outcome: Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.
why: Both require periodic review to be planned, with the owner and the frequency defined.

title: Name an owner and review this policy on a schedule
outcome: Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.
why: Naming one policy owner documents one role; the subcategory covers roles and communication lines more widely.

title: Name an owner and review this policy on a schedule
outcome: Review of the AI policy
why: The control is titled review of the AI policy, which is what the rule requires, on a stated schedule.

title: Name an owner and review this policy on a schedule
outcome: AI roles and responsibilities
why: Naming a policy owner assigns one AI role; the control covers defining AI roles and responsibilities generally.
